source.title: On the geometry of generalization and memorization in deep neural networks
source.authors: Cory Stephenson; Suchismita Padhy; Abhinav Ganesh; Yue Hui; Hanlin Tang; SueYeon Chung

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided, including supplemental information.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the coexistence of fitting randomized training labels and generalization on natural labels, and tests how model size relates to test accuracy and representation geometry using its own experiments.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported accuracy results, layer rewinding outcomes, model-size double descent, and measured manifold and gradient properties. Cited results from other work are excluded. Numerous plot values are described qualitatively rather than reported numerically.
record.test_reason: The study measures fitting randomized training labels alongside generalization to natural-label test examples in new architectures and datasets, bearing on V1. Its width experiment reports double descent but does not identify the zero-training-error threshold needed to test V2's post-interpolation claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors locate memorization mainly in deeper layers and later epochs, describe early learning of shared features, demonstrate recovery through individual late-layer rewinding, and associate model-size double descent with nonmonotonic manifold dimensionality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mixed-label permutation rather than fitting a fully randomized-label dataset; analyzes layerwise manifold geometry and gradient contributions, and includes selective layer rewinding. Networks use Adam, learning rate 1 × 10−4, batch size 1,024, with no weight decay or other regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with training epoch, layer depth, model architecture and size, dataset, and fraction of permuted labels. The paper states that Tiny ImageNet training reached only partial memorization after 1,000 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Restored and test representations have similar geometry at peak generalization; memorization later changes predominantly deep-layer geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With mixed correct and randomized labels, early representations retain shared class features while late layers increasingly encode randomized labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Rewinding individual late layers recovers substantial test accuracy after prolonged training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing selected late-layer weights with earlier values can recover generalization lost during memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Width-scaled ResNet18 exhibits double descent in test accuracy and nonmonotonic test-manifold dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On CIFAR-100 with 10% label noise, model-size double descent accompanies nonmonotonic representation dimensionality.

fits_no_version.finding: Early layers do not have vanishing gradients; correctly labeled examples initially dominate the label-dependent gradient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared features preferentially drive early learning in networks trained on mixed correct and randomized labels.

record.problems: The central accuracy and geometry trends are mostly presented in figures, with many results described qualitatively rather than numerically in the text. The study uses CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet, not the specific datasets and architectures named in several claim versions. It uses Adam and a large batch size, and states these hyperparameters were not optimized for generalization. Some Tiny ImageNet runs only partially memorize.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying distinct outcomes omitted. Numerous separate layerwise manifold measurements in Figures 3 and A.5-A.8 are presented as plots without textual numerical values; included only where the paper states a summarized qualitative result. Rewinding curves in Figures A.9-A.11 likewise lack textual numeric outcomes beyond the qualitative summaries recorded above.

untested.parts: The complete matched-recipe comparison of natural-label training against fully randomized-label training, including chance-level held-out accuracy after random-label fitting; the original named architectures and datasets; and an unambiguous no-explicit-regularization condition for VGG16.
Test-error changes specifically beyond the width required for zero training error, with training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers under comparable training, including local-connectivity explanations.
Comparative generalization of adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Controlled effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Separate training and held-out accuracy outcomes for AlexNet and ResNet18 on CIFAR-100, and ResNet18 on Tiny ImageNet. The text explicitly distinguishes incomplete Tiny ImageNet memorization after 1000 epochs from the near-perfect fits elsewhere; R1 records only VGG16.

The synthetic-data feedforward network's training and test accuracy results provide another architecture and setting bearing on coexistence. The text reports accuracy trends similar to the main experiments, but no row captures them.

record.verdict_notes: Declining test accuracy during prolonged training does not itself limit V1: V1 does not assert that memorization leaves test accuracy unchanged. Geometry and rewinding results therefore cannot justify the record's V1 limits_scope verdict. Numerical plot values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text alone.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the specific same-recipe, random-label held-out chance-accuracy comparison on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, or the named Zhang et al. architectures.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with 50% randomly permuted labels, without weight decay or other regularization; evaluated training and test accuracy over epochs.
rows.value: near 100% training accuracy; test accuracy eventually decreases
rows.note: The text does not provide exact accuracy values in prose. This shows memorization and declining test performance, but does not state the held-out accuracy relative to chance.
rows.check: Supports coexistence in a partially randomized dataset; it does not establish the full clean-label versus fully randomized-label comparison. The claim of no regularization needs qualification: Table 3 lists dropout in VGG16, despite the experimental-setup statement.

source_check.correct: Near-100% training accuracy and eventual test-accuracy decline are reported. Section 3 states no weight decay or other regularization, but Appendix A.10, Table 3 lists BatchNorm and two Dropout layers in VGG16; qualify the unregularized-training description because the paper is internally inconsistent.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Figure 2A and opening Results paragraph; Figure 4A–B caption; Appendix A.10, Table 3.
source_check.problem: The unqualified absence of other regularization conflicts with the specified VGG16 architecture.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with 50% randomly permuted labels; compared accuracy on unpermuted, permuted, and restored training examples.
rows.measure: Accuracy on unpermuted, permuted, and restored training examples
rows.value: Permuted examples take more epochs to fit, then quickly converge; restored-example accuracy rises before permuted examples are learned and later declines.
rows.note: Restored examples use the correct labels for examples whose training labels were permuted; these are training examples, not held-out test examples.
rows.check: Bears on fitting randomized labels. Restored-example accuracy concerns training inputs and cannot establish held-out generalization.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V1 from this row alone. Permuted examples require more epochs to fit and then converge quickly; restored-example accuracy initially increases. These measurements concern training inputs and establish components of memorization, not held-out generalization.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1 example definitions; Figure 2A, right; opening Results paragraphs.
source_check.problem: Observed training-subset behavior alone cannot establish V1's coexistence with held-out generalization.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Compared manifold capacity for test and restored examples at the best-generalizing epoch and final epoch of training.
rows.measure: Manifold capacity and geometry of test and restored-example representations
rows.value: Restored and test manifolds show no significant differences; both become more separable in deeper layers.
rows.note: Representation geometry supports shared class features but is not itself a report of held-out accuracy above chance.
rows.check: Manifold capacity and geometry do not measure the accuracy comparison V1 names.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Compared manifold capacity for test and restored examples at the best-generalizing epoch and final epoch of training.
rows.measure: Manifold capacity and geometry of restored and test-example representations
rows.value: Restored manifolds have decreased capacity compared with the best epoch; restored and test manifolds show similar trends but diverge from unpermuted manifolds after layer 14.
rows.note: Memorization in later layers is associated with degraded restored-example geometry. No exact held-out accuracy is stated here.
rows.check: Changes in representation geometry do not establish failure of coexistence between memorization capacity and generalization.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Rewound parameters of one layer in a model trained for 1000 epochs to values from an earlier epoch; final three linear layers were not rewound.
rows.baseline: peak generalization performance from early stopping
rows.value: >90% as accurate as the best early-stopped model
rows.note: Rewinding partially restores test performance after memorization. The paper does not give the exact accuracy value in prose.
rows.check: Selective weight rewinding tests recovery of generalization, not V1. The operation is parameter replacement, not removal of training examples.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Rewound one layer's parameters in a model trained for 1000 epochs to earlier values.
rows.baseline: peak generalization performance obtained by early stopping
rows.value: Rewinding the last layer corrects a significant fraction of the decrease in test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 10 training runs with different random seeds
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the text; no numeric test accuracy is given.
rows.check: Selective weight rewinding tests recovery of generalization, not a listed version. The operation is parameter replacement.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Rewound one layer's parameters in a model trained for 1000 epochs to earlier values.
rows.baseline: peak generalization performance obtained by early stopping
rows.value: Final two layers show an effect as in VGG16.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 4 training runs with different random seeds
rows.note: The text states similarity to the VGG16 rewinding effect but gives no numeric value.
rows.check: Selective weight rewinding tests recovery of generalization, not a listed version. The final two layers are rewound individually, not necessarily together.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.size_stated: varied by scaling layer width; parameter counts not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Scaled common layer width to vary parameter count and trained on CIFAR-100 with 10% label noise.
rows.measure: Model accuracy at best and final epochs
rows.value: Model accuracy exhibits double descent as parameter count increases.
rows.note: The study explicitly reports double descent but does not give accuracy values in prose. It does not establish zero training error at each width.
rows.check: Double descent in test accuracy does not establish V1 or locate V2's width threshold for zero training error. The supplied text does not show whether the worsening region precedes or follows interpolation.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.size_stated: varied by scaling layer width; parameter counts not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Measured test-data manifold geometry across model sizes at the final epoch and best epoch.
rows.value: At the final epoch, dimensionality first decreases, then increases, and decreases again with larger model size.
rows.note: The authors state radius and center correlation have monotonic relationships similar to the best epoch; this row records the reported non-monotonic dimension pattern.
rows.check: Manifold dimension is neither held-out accuracy nor magnitude-aware weight sharpness; it does not test V1, V2 or V7.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient norms by layer and epoch for all, unpermuted, and permuted samples.
rows.measure: Gradient norm across layers and epochs
rows.value: Gradients do not vanish in early layers; unpermuted and permuted examples contribute similarly to the total gradient during the last training phase.
rows.note: This measures gradient magnitude, not held-out error or test accuracy.
rows.check: Gradient magnitudes test a proposed mechanism, not any listed version's outcome.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Compared label-dependent and label-independent gradient contributions from unpermuted and permuted examples over training.
rows.value: Initially, the label-dependent gradient contribution from unpermuted examples is significantly larger than from permuted examples.
rows.note: Gradient contribution is a proposed mechanism for learning dynamics, not a direct test-error measure.
rows.check: Gradient decomposition tests a proposed mechanism, not any listed version's outcome.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: VGG-16 trained on CIFAR-100 with 50% randomly permuted labels
reader_labels.reason: The network approaches near-100% training accuracy while test accuracy initially generalizes before declining; restored and test representations show similar geometry at peak generalization (R1-R3). The paper does not report the version's exact held-out chance comparison.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Late training after memorization; layer rewinding
reader_labels.reason: Memorization coincides with degraded restored-example geometry and declining test performance, while rewinding the final convolutional layer recovers more than 90% of best early-stopped accuracy (R4-R5).
